<description>
With the change on #36895 :
[quoted text omitted]

This adds `btck_witness_stack_get_items` which reads the stack in one O(n) pass and writes each item's pointer and size into two arrays passed to it. `WitnessStackApi::GetItems` is the C++ wrapper. The pointers are valid as long as the witness stack exists.

An earlier version passed each item to a callback from the bottom of the stack to the top. That order followed the serialization, which can only be read from the bottom up, more than how a stack should actually be read. This version lets the items be read from either end.
</description>

This processes the witness stack from the bottom to the top, treating it more like a queue than a stack. Doesn't really feel the right API to me?

On second thought / glance a call that writes every item's pointer and size into two arrays passed to it, so the items can be read from either end might be the better shape for the API.
